description: 🚀 Team PANDAM is a student-led team using AI, NASA Earth observation data, and satellite technology to solve agricultural and environmental challenges. We welcome members interested in AI, software development, data science, GIS, design, and sustainability.
summary:
Team Pandam built two connected prototypes for the Field Shift challenge in Bangladesh.
AgriLume Time Travel is a bilingual (Bangla/English) 3D and VR web simulator. It lets farmers and
advisers compare observed NASA POWER weather history (Rajshahi, 2001-2025) with clearly
labelled what-if futures, using NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 projection deltas for Bangladesh's 64
district centres. It runs on PC, phones, Cardboard and WebXR headsets, with a 2D fallback, voice
commands, live captions and optional hand-gesture controls. AgriGuardian is a companion Flutter
app with a FastAPI and PostGIS backend. It resolves any of Bangladesh's 64 districts, retrieves the
regional BAMIS crop calendar and compares crop-rotation scenarios using NASA POWER rainfall
and temperature, FAO GAEZ suitability and irrigation access. It reports evidence gaps instead of
inventing values. Every number is labelled observed, what-if or simulator, and yield is a relative
index, not a forecast. Both are prototypes that still need agronomist review, real-device testing and
farmer pilots.
details:
Our project, AgriLume and AgriGuardian, aims to help Bangladeshi farmers understand climate change, explore historical weather patterns, and make better-informed agricultural decisions.

The project has two main prototypes: a 3D interactive web platform and a mobile agricultural decision-support application.

1. The Problem We Identified

Bangladeshi farmers face challenges when selecting crops and deciding the right planting time because rainfall and temperature change every year.

Unpredictable rainfall, extreme heat, and changing weather conditions can affect crop growth, agricultural planning, and food production.

To understand this problem, we analysed NASA POWER daily climate data (2001–2025) for Rajshahi.

Our analysis found:

Minimum June–September rainfall: 693 mm in 2003.

Maximum June–September rainfall: 1,335 mm in 2019.

25-year average rainfall: 990 mm.

Days with maximum temperatures of 40°C or higher ranged from 0 days in 2018 and 2020 to 41 days in 2010.

These differences show why farmers need better access to historical climate information and possible future climate scenarios.

Our solution helps farmers explore these climate variations before the farming season instead of reacting after problems occur.

2. Our Main Solutions

Our project consists of two connected prototypes.

A. AgriLume Time Travel (Web Platform)

Elevating Event Experiences with WebAR and AR Apps

AgriLume Time Travel is a 3D interactive agricultural web platform that allows users to explore historical weather conditions and labelled future climate scenarios.

Users can select a district and a year to understand how climate conditions may affect agricultural environments.

Key Features:

1. Historical Climate Exploration: Displays NASA POWER historical rainfall and temperature records from 2001 to 2025.

2. Future Climate Scenarios: Uses NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 projections from two climate models, GFDL-CM4 and GISS-E2-1-G.

3. 64 District Coverage: The bundled projection dataset covers 64 district centres.

4. 3D Farm Environment: Provides an interactive 3D farming experience directly in a web browser.

5. Climate Comparison: Allows users to compare historical weather observations with labelled what-if future scenarios.

6. Yield Simulation: Displays a relative yield index with a baseline of 100. It is an educational indicator, not an actual yield forecast.

7. VR Support: Supports Cardboard mode and WebXR-compatible headsets.

8. Mobile Accessibility: Supports touchscreen and gyroscope controls on mobile devices.

9. Bilingual Assistant: Provides Bangla and English voice and text interaction through an offline rule-based assistant. It is not an LLM.

10. Hand Gesture Controls: Supports eight optional camera-based hand gestures using MediaPipe Hands. These controls are not Bangla Sign Language translation.

11. Emergency Support: Emergency phrases can be directed to Bangladesh's national emergency service, 999.

12. Additional Resources: Includes a NASA dataset registry, official Bangladesh agricultural agency links, straw and husk recycling estimates, and an educational farming game.

The platform also provides a 2D fallback for devices that do not support WebGL.

B. AgriGuardian (Mobile Application + Backend)

SARAI CeNTRO

xFarm: La soluzione completa per l'azienda agricola

Agriculture Mobile App UI/UX Design :: Behance

12

AgriGuardian is a mobile agricultural decision-support application designed to help farmers and agricultural advisers compare possible crop rotations using available agricultural and climate information.

It combines location information, regional crop calendars, historical climate data, and crop suitability information.

Key Features:

1. Mobile Application: Developed using Flutter and Dart.

2. Bilingual Onboarding: Supports both Bangla and English.

3. Location Identification: Uses GPS coordinates or field boundaries to identify the relevant district.

4. Crop Calendar Integration: Uses regional crop calendars from BAMIS.

5. Crop Rotation Comparison: Compares feasible crop rotations using calendar overlap, available water evidence, irrigation access, and supported farmer priorities.

6. Climate Analysis: Uses NASA POWER daily rainfall and temperature records.

7. Crop Suitability: Uses FAO GAEZ for crop suitability screening and tie-breaking.

8. Soil and Climate Context: Provides NASA POWER climatology and ISRIC SoilGrids information as additional context.

9. Evidence Transparency: Clearly reports when important agricultural information is missing.

10. Rajshahi Aman Pilot: Blocks actionable planting-date recommendations until its methodology passes transfer validation.

The backend is built using FastAPI, PostgreSQL and PostGIS, with Redis, Alembic and Firebase Authentication.

Our project combines information from several scientific and agricultural data sources.

Important data limitation: NASA POWER provides satellite and model-based grid data at approximately 0.5° × 0.625° resolution. It does not provide exact measurements for individual agricultural fields.

We also distinguish between historical observations, future projections, and simulator outputs to avoid confusing different types of information.

5. What Makes Our Project Creative and Innovative?

The most important innovation of our project is the concept of Time as an Interactive Interface.

Instead of presenting climate information only through traditional charts and tables, we allow users to explore agricultural environments through different time periods.

For example, users can explore the same agricultural field under:

Historical rainfall conditions.

Historical temperature conditions.

Different years of climate records.

Labelled future climate scenarios.

Educational farming simulations.

Our main innovations include:

1. Climate Time Travel

Users can explore past and possible future climate conditions in one interactive environment.

2. 3D Agricultural Visualization

We transform climate information into an interactive 3D farming experience.

3. Virtual Reality Accessibility

Users can explore agricultural environments through compatible VR devices.

4. Bilingual Communication

The platform supports Bangla and English interaction to make information more accessible.

5. Gesture-Based Interaction

Users can interact with the platform using eight optional hand gestures.

6. Evidence Transparency

Each number is identified as observed, what-if, or simulator information. Missing evidence is also displayed instead of being replaced with unsupported assumptions.

6. Benefits and Expected Impact

Our project aims to support farmers, agricultural advisers, and people interested in climate-smart agriculture.

Expected Benefits:

Better understanding of changing rainfall and temperature patterns.

Improved awareness of agricultural climate risks.

Easier comparison of historical and possible future climate conditions.

Better-informed discussions about crop selection.

Better understanding of possible planting windows.

Improved access to agricultural information in Bangla and English.

Greater awareness of technology-supported farming.

Increased accessibility through mobile, PC, and compatible VR devices.

Our main objective is to support better-prepared agricultural decisions, not to replace farmers or automatically make farming decisions for them.

7. Factors We Considered During Development

We considered several important factors while designing and developing the project.

Accessibility: Bangla and English language support, voice interaction, captions, mobile accessibility, Cardboard compatibility, and 2D fallback.

Data Accuracy: NASA POWER provides regional grid-based information, not exact individual-field measurements.

Safety: Emergency phrases are directed to 999, while official weather and disaster warnings refer users to BMD, FFWC, and DDM.

Transparency: Historical observations, future projections, and simulator outputs are clearly distinguished.

Responsible Technology: We avoid presenting unverified information as scientific fact or claiming guaranteed agricultural results.

8. Testing and Current Limitations

92 Automated Tests Passed

We have completed several technical testing activities for the web application.

Completed Testing:

Successful web application build.

Lint checks passed.

92 automated tests passed.

Tested using headless Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

Checked using desktop and mobile device emulation.

Current Limitations:

The application has not yet been tested on a physical VR headset.

Physical mobile devices and iPhone Safari have not yet been tested.

The crop model is educational and uncalibrated.

No agronomist or farmer review has been completed.

No learner pilot has been conducted.

Browser voice interaction usually requires an online service.

Bangla voices may not be available on all devices.

No Bangla Sign Language clips are included.

AgriGuardian's crop rotation service is currently a backend capability, and the complete farmer-facing workflow has not yet been verified.

Some weather and satellite showcase screens contain labelled demo content.

We do not claim field-level accuracy, guaranteed crop yields, or scientifically validated agricultural recommendations.

12. Overall Project Summary

AgriLume + AgriGuardian

Climate-Aware Agricultural Decision Support for Bangladesh

Aerial photography

AgriLume Time Travel helps users understand historical and possible future climate conditions through 3D visualization, interactive simulations, and VR experiences.

AgriGuardian helps farmers and agricultural advisers compare possible crop rotations using regional crop calendars, climate history, and available agricultural evidence.

Together, these two prototypes aim to make agricultural climate information more understandable, accessible, and useful for better-informed farming decisions.

Our Vision

"Building a smarter, more climate-aware, and technology-supported agricultural future for Bangladesh."

TEAM PANDAM · NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE 2026

Final Message:

Our project is not simply a weather application or a farming game. It combines NASA climate data, agricultural information, 3D visualization, virtual reality, mobile technology, and evidence-based decision support into one connected concept.

We want to help farmers understand what happened, explore what could happen, and prepare better for what comes next.
